answer: A farm running 126 keys hence forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. Because the dawn stake is held until the sparrow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the island audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 12% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
